archetypes.name: sourcing-root-split
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a SCRIPT_ROOT/PLUGIN_ROOT split that must be applied consistently across three consumers with different execution contexts; the static panel is unlikely to catch the subtle cross-consumer path invariants.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan adds scripts/lib-sparse-dirs.sh as a sourced-only library and requires each consumer to source it from SCRIPT_ROOT (the executing script's own tree), never from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or PLUGIN_ROOT. Verify that the plan's upgrade-larch.sh changes correctly separate SCRIPT_ROOT (new, for lib-sparse-dirs.sh) from PLUGIN_ROOT (kept, for lib-quiet.sh, cache math, and prune), and that the two roots diverge as intended when /release invokes the working-tree script with an explicit CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT pointing at a different cache root. Check the sessionstart-health.sh probe section: the plan says to source from SCRIPT_DIR or a locally-bound plugin root, but sessionstart-health.sh already sources lib-quiet.sh from $SCRIPT_DIR/lib-quiet.sh (line 21) — verify whether adding the lib-sparse-dirs.sh source via the same SCRIPT_DIR path is actually correct given that lib-sparse-dirs.sh lives in scripts/ while the hook lives in scripts/ too (same directory), and whether any path-resolution difference emerges under the stripped-PATH env-i test harness. Also check whether the agent-lint.toml dead-script G004 exclusion pattern the plan specifies is syntactically consistent with the existing entries for other sourced-only libraries. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: release-cone-detection
archetypes.rationale: The plan's CONE_RECONCILED state handoff between release Step 7 and Step 8 relies on parsing larch_err output that goes to stderr, not stdout; this is a concrete specifiability gap the static panel's Requirements/Pragmatic reviewers may overlook because it requires tracing the quiet-lib output routing.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan requires /release Step 7 to detect whether a same-version sparse-cone reconcile occurred by parsing the upgrade script's output for a sentinel line, then persist a CONE_RECONCILED boolean for Step 8 to act on. Verify whether the sentinel line the plan quotes ('Already at latest stable ... sparse checkout is out of date ... Reconciling ...') is emitted via larch_err, which routes to stderr after larch_quiet_init (see upgrade-larch.sh lines 7-10 and lib-quiet.sh), and therefore whether a plain bash capture of the working-tree script would miss it unless stderr is explicitly redirected in the Step 7 invocation shape. Check whether the plan's Step 7 command form (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=... bash ...upgrade-larch.sh) includes any stderr capture or redirect, and whether 'and/or treat a same-version reinstall path as cone reconcile' provides a robust fallback or introduces a new ambiguity when the version-match + cone-drift path also reinstalls. Also verify that the CONE_RECONCILED → Step 8 restart coupling is actionable given that SKILL.md is an instruction document: does the plan describe a concrete mechanism (env var, exit code, log file) for persisting this state across SKILL.md steps, or does it assume narrative context will carry it? Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: home-fixture-isolation
archetypes.rationale: MARKETPLACE_CLONE is bound at source time from $HOME (upgrade-larch.sh line 22), so test cases that source the script without first isolating HOME will silently hit the developer's real marketplace or vacuously pass; the plan calls this out but the proposed harness changes must actually close the gap.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan mandates per-case HOME isolation before sourcing upgrade-larch.sh because MARKETPLACE_CLONE is assigned at script-source time (skills/upgrade-larch/scripts/upgrade-larch.sh line 22) and is therefore fixed the moment the file is sourced. Verify that the plan's test-upgrade-larch-retention.sh changes correctly sequence the HOME export and fixture creation before every source call, including the new already_latest_and_cone_ok cases and the release-style RC1 guard case. Check whether the dual-update LARCH_SPARSE_DIRS literal guard the plan describes is scoped as a hard-coded expected string (e.g. assert actual == '.claude .claude-plugin ...') rather than importing lib-sparse-dirs.sh and asserting lib_value == lib_value — a lib-vs-itself tautology that the plan explicitly warns against but whose test structure is not fully specified. For test-sessionstart-health.sh, verify whether the plan's 'thread HOME through run_from_dir / run_with_stdin' instruction is sufficient given that the harness uses env -i: does env -i strip HOME before the hook subprocess starts, and does the plan specify the exact env -i invocation shape needed to re-inject HOME? Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
